resources.string: Shear rate = relative speed ÷ film thickness. Multiplying that rate by an example viscosity of 0.01 Pa·s gives the model shear stress.

Pleural fluid helps the two pleural surfaces slide during breathing. This example uses ideal parallel surfaces and a fictional fluid viscosity; the lower surface is the model reference. It does not measure pleural fluid, pressure, or breathing performance.
The chest-wall side moves relative to the lung side. The film is magnified for illustration. Model shear rate: %1$s per second.
